high.title: Thai Investors Withdraw Capital from Vietnam's Two Largest ETFs
high.summary: Foreign investors continued their prolonged net selling trend on Vietnam's stock market. From the beginning of 2026, foreign investors have net sold over VND 62,000 billion on HoSE, continuing the record VND 125,000 billion outflow from last year. Part of this foreign capital withdrawal belongs to Thai investors. Through depositary receipts (DR), Thai investors have heavily net sold two Vietnamese ETF certificates: DCVFM VN30 ETF (E1VFVN30) and DCVFM VNDiamond ETF (FUEVFVND). As of May 25, DR E1VFVN3001 holdings decreased by 11.8 million units since the beginning of the year to just over 90.4 million units, equivalent to market capitalization of less than 4 billion Baht (~VND 3,200 billion). This sustained foreign outflow pressure signals continued challenges for VND stability and Vietnamese equity markets, as ETF redemptions can amplify selling pressure on underlying holdings.

high.title: High Savings Interest Rates Soar to Peak Levels
high.summary: In the final days of May, the deposit mobilization market became more active as commercial banks simultaneously launched attractive high savings interest rate programs. VIB is applying rates up to 8.35%/year for deposits with terms from 6-11 months, with additional incentives for online deposits versus counter deposits. Sacombank also deployed deposit mobilization programs with rates up to over 8%/year for 6-12 month term deposits. VPBank and SeABank maintain savings packages with rates of 8.5-8.9%/year for medium and long-term periods. This aggressive rate competition indicates banks are struggling to attract deposits back into the system, potentially signaling liquidity pressures that could impact lending growth and monetary policy transmission.

high.title: VietABank Prepares for Capital Increase
high.summary: VietABank's Board of Directors approved the first capital increase plan for 2026 through issuing shares from owner's equity. The bank plans to issue over 122.45 million shares to existing shareholders at a 15% ratio. Total issuance value at par value is expected to reach nearly VND 1,225 billion. If completed in Q2-Q3/2026, VietABank's charter capital will increase from nearly VND 8,164 billion to about VND 9,388 billion. This capital injection strengthens the bank's financial foundation for lending expansion and regulatory compliance amid tightening capital adequacy requirements.

medium.title: SBV Payment Department Chief Clarifies Transaction Splitting Rules
medium.summary: State Bank of Vietnam's Payment Department Head clarified that SBV does not prohibit transaction splitting for transfers over VND 500 million, countering market confusion about prolonged processing times. However, splitting transactions while only performing biometric authentication once violates regulations.

medium.title: SJC Gold Prices Fall in Afternoon Session May 27
medium.summary: On May 27, domestic gold prices fell sharply by VND 800,000/tael compared to the previous day. SJC Company quoted gold bars at VND 157.7-160.7 million/tael, down VND 800,000/tael in both buying and selling directions. International gold prices also declined to near $4,500/ounce.

medium.title: MSB Bank Shares Surge Near Historical High
medium.summary: MSB shares of Maritime Bank continued attracting attention in the May 27 morning session, rising 2.39% to VND 15,000/share, approaching the historical high set in early September 2025. Foreign investors continued net buying over 3 million shares in the session.

medium.title: ACBS Securities to Increase Capital by Additional VND 2,000 Billion
medium.summary: ACB Securities (ACBS) announced that ACB's Board of Directors approved increasing ACBS's charter capital by VND 2,000 billion, from VND 11,000 billion to VND 13,000 billion. ACBS is a wholly-owned subsidiary of ACB, chaired by Tran Hung Huy.
